name: Autosomal Recessive Palmoplantar Keratoderma and Congenital Alopecia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Autosomal Recessive Palmoplantar Keratoderma and Congenital Alopecia

criteria.description: Presence of congenital alopecia evident at birth or shortly thereafter
Diffuse or focal hyperkeratosis of the palms and soles developing in infancy or early childhood
Family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance or confirmed pathogenic variants in associated genes
Presence of nail abnormalities such as dystrophic or absent nails
Lack of systemic features differentiating from syndromic keratodermas

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital alopecia and palmoplantar keratoderma with autosomal recessive inheritance pattern or confirmed genetic mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended to confirm diagnosis and exclude overlapping syndromes.

laboratory: Histopathology showing epidermal hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as GJB2 (connexin 26) or other keratin-related genes associated with autosomal recessive palmoplantar keratoderma and alopecia
other: Family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Hair shaft abnormalities without palmoplantar keratoderma
Normal nails and skin on palms and soles
Palmoplantar keratoderma with nail dystrophy and alopecia but with additional nail and hair abnormalities
Presence of other ectodermal dysplasia features

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin fissures with secondary infection
Development of systemic symptoms such as fever or malaise
Family history of syndromic keratoderma with multisystem involvement
references: Orphanet: Autosomal recessive palmoplantar keratoderma and congenital alopecia - ORPHA1366
